findings: l.3136/l.3157: Omega_lox(Gamma) is called 'the convex domain' but is not convex: for Gamma = <gamma> it is U+(gamma) disjoint union U-(gamma) (interior_achronalDomain_eq_quadrants). The proof l.3157-3165 is valid on each Gamma-invariant convex piece, hence on Omega^+-(Lambda(Gamma)).

The printed statement l.3143-3144 is nevertheless TRUE (proved, blem_sanlox), by an argument the paper does not give: no x in U_lox(Gamma) lies in a future quadrant U+(gamma) and a past quadrant U-(gamma') (not_mem_quadrantPlus_quadrantMinus). Choose the repulsive point w of gamma^{+-1} whose direction differs from the attractive direction of gamma'; some gamma'^m x crosses the hyperplane of w (exists_lt_minkB_pow_smul, the orbit's null coordinate grows like lambda'^{-m}); then gamma^{+-n} gamma'^m x - x is timelike for n large (exists_minkQ_neg_of_sign: in the null frame of gamma, |z|^2 = 2 f(z) g(z)/<n|n'> + |v(z)|^2, f(z) ~ lambda^{-n}, g(z) -> -g(x), and the transverse part v grows at most linearly, minkQ_nullV_pow_smul_sub_le). An element of Gamma with a timelike displacement is loxodromic under Rem 8.9 (a linear parabolic displaces into J^perp, which has Q >= 0; a spacelike elliptic or tangent parabolic has Omega_g = M^n), and x is not in its achronal domain (not_minkQ_neg_of_mem_UGammaLox). Hence Omega_lox(Gamma) is contained in Omega+(Lambda(Gamma)) union Omega-(Lambda(Gamma)), both in Omega(Gamma): there are no mixed-sign components, and the paper's case analysis of linear parabolics on Omega_lox is only ever needed on the one-sided pieces.

l.3159-3163 ('the convex hull of the gamma0-orbit of x is a complete lightlike line'): replaced by an exact growth argument <n|gamma^k x> = <n|c> + <n|R^k y> + k<n|p(y)>; a point of P(gamma0) in ker p has a bounded orbit, so x must first be moved off ker p inside the open set (done).

Cartan's theorem was NOT needed as an external: its local form (the neutral component of a closed subgroup of SO0(1,d) is open in it) is proved in Flat/Lox/ClosedSubgroupNhds by the elementary von Neumann argument in the finite-dimensional Banach algebra End(M^n): (a) exp X_k in S, X_k -> 0, X_k/|X_k| -> Y gives exp(tY) in S (floor multiples); (b) h = {Y | forall t, exp(tY) in S} is closed under addition (Trotter, via the derivative Y+Z at 0 of s |-> log(exp(sY)exp(sZ)), log = HasStrictFDerivAt.localInverse of exp); (c) with a complement m of h, (H,M) |-> exp H exp M is a local homeomorphism at 0 (inverse function theorem), and a bad sequence would give a unit vector of h ∩ m; (d) SO0(1,d) is closed in End(M^n) (Q-preserving, future-preserving, det 1 are closed conditions; det 1 gives invertibility, LinearMap.equivOfIsUnitDet).

findings: l.3326-3330: the conclusion 'M(S) = Gamma\Omega(S~) is a linear twisted product over a Misner spacetime' is false for Gamma itself; it holds up to finite index. Counterexample in M^4 (form xy+|z|^2, coordinates (x,z1,z2,y)): gamma0(x,z,y) = (e^-1 x, z, e y), sigma(x,z1,z2,y) = (-y, z1+1, -z2, -x) (SO0-affine, spacelike elliptic, allowed by Rem 8.9), sigma gamma0 sigma^-1 = gamma0^-1; Gamma = <gamma0, sigma> acts freely and properly on Omega = {x>0,y<0} x R^2, Sigma = {xy=-1} ∩ Omega satisfies (CC'), Omega(S~) = Omega; <gamma0, sigma^2> has index 2 and fixes Delta_0, so Gamma is elementary; the direction of U contains the (x,y)-plane, so Gamma_U is non-abelian, while a Misner group (misnerGroup L) is abelian, and quotient presentations of a convex domain are conjugate. Found by the read-only audit; statement restated for a finite-index Gamma'.

l.3320-3321: 'As in corollary abel, we see that the action on pi_P^-1(0) is free and properly discontinuous' is FALSE for Gamma (true for Gamma0 = ker a). Counterexample in M^4 (form xy+|z|^2, z in R^2): gamma0(x,z,y) = (e^-1 x, R_theta z, e y), theta/pi irrational, Gamma = <gamma0>: elementary (fixes both null axes), loxodromic, free and proper on Omega = {x>0,y<0} x R^2 and on the (CC') surface {xy=-1} ∩ Omega; but gamma0 acts on pi_P^-1(0) = {x=y=0} = R^2 by the rotation R_theta, which fixes 0 and has dense orbits on circles. [10.M]'s conclusion still holds there (U' = {z=0}: a Misner spacetime in M^2), so the statement loxo_elementary_misner is not refuted; the Bieberbach step must be run for Gamma0 (normalised by Gamma).

closer, 2026-11-01: loxo_elementary_misner as stated (no BieberbachI hypothesis) implies Bieberbach I for torsion-free orientation-preserving crystallographic groups of R^{d'} (sketch in the obstruction), so it cannot be closed in this library without either a formal Bieberbach I or a statement change adding hBieb (as nonloxodromic_* carry). The statement is NOT false (Bieberbach I is a theorem). Recommendation for the master: add (hBieb : ∀ k : ℕ, k ≤ d' + 1 → BieberbachI (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin k))), discharged where nonloxodromic's is.
